title: Strict augmentation data from finite-piece bar diagrams
statement: Let Y be a scheme and P,Pprime complexes of module sheaves [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], both actual flat telescopes [def-sc-flat-telescope-stage-map], with f:P→Pprime. There are bounded-above termwise-flat towers E0,E1,E2 and level maps a:E0→E1,b:E0→E2 with strict sum squares for the telescope differentials. There are compatible quasi-isomorphisms qn:E0n→τ≤nP [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules]. There are target maps r1:Tel(E1)→P,r2:Tel(E2)→Pprime inducing homotopy-category isomorphisms and having zero shifted-summand restrictions. For s=Σdesc(qn;ιn), their unshifted restrictions satisfy Σmap(a);inr;r1=s and Σmap(b);inr;r2=s;f strictly. No source-cone augmentation or equality of maps from it is asserted.

source.place: 03EW flat-generator covers; 077J/06XX split generator-valued truncation tower; parent geometric construction expanded by the agent using finite subcomplexes and bar enlargement.

proof.text: Choose E,t,q by the flat truncation tower theorem and set p_n=q_n followed by the good truncation inclusion into P. Its compatibility is exactly the tower compatibility.

Apply the one-target refinement to E,t,p with target P, obtaining R,s,c,F,u,a and r1. Apply it again to R,s with augmentation c_n;p_n;f and target Pprime. The second application yields S,v,d,G,w,b and r2. Compatibility of its input follows by associativity and s_n;c_(n+1)=c_n;t_n.

Use S,F,G and level maps d_n;a_n,b_n. A level square induces the telescope sum square: test on each coproduct inclusion, distribute 1-shift, and use the level identity. Compose the sum square of d with that of a. Define qprime_n=d_n;c_n;q_n. Quasi-isomorphisms compose; applying the two refinement naturality identities followed by the original truncation compatibility proves strict compatibility of qprime.

Retain r1,r2 and their homotopy-category isomorphisms and zero shifted restrictions. Test each of the final two sum identities on its nth coproduct inclusion. The first becomes d_n;a_n;inr;r1=d_n;c_n;p_n; the second becomes b_n;inr;r2=d_n;c_n;p_n;f. These are the two refinement augmentation identities with composition reassociated.

proof_origin.place: Successive one-target refinements and the proved telescope sum-square calculation; geometric finite-piece bar construction retained in the one-target lemma.
